caveats: Observational: launches in busier weeks got fewer or more reviews on average, after adjusting for the listed controls. It does not show that a busy week causes it.
Pre-launch hype (wishlists, followers) drives both reviews and the choice of week. Until most launches have a follower count, the headline fit has no hype control (see followers).
Reviews stand in for sales; the ratio of sales to reviews varies by genre and price.
Price, demo, tags and Early Access state are today's, not launch day's.
Games delisted before the data was collected are missing, so older years look a bit better than they were.

cn_spring.label: launch during China's Spring Festival holiday (games with Simplified Chinese: main effect times extra)

cn_national.label: launch during China's National Day holiday (games with Simplified Chinese: main effect times extra)

holidays.note: Chinese holidays (rate ratios, 95% intervals): Spring Festival: games without Simplified Chinese 36% fewer reviews (0.64 (0.47 to 0.87)), games with it no clear difference (0.76 (0.58 to 1.01)); the chance test (all games pooled) gives 0.73 with p = 0.097; National Day: games without Simplified Chinese 57% fewer reviews (0.43 (0.28 to 0.67)), games with it 52% fewer reviews (0.48 (0.24 to 0.94)); the chance test (all games pooled) gives 0.50 with p = 0.005. In the review-count model the extra effect of Simplified Chinese is 1.20 (0.80 to 1.78) for Spring Festival and 1.10 (0.64 to 1.90) for National Day: no clear difference, but the intervals are wide, so a difference is not ruled out. In the "any reviews" part, games with Simplified Chinese launched during Spring Festival were less likely to get any review than other games launched then (extra odds ratio 0.72 (0.56 to 0.93)). 9 of the 9 holiday windows overlapped another Steam event (a sale, Next Fest or a themed fest), and there are only 5 Spring Festival and 4 National Day windows, so the week-clustered intervals overstate how sure this is. Not a general rule.
holidays.site_use: Show Chinese holidays only as calendar context for games that support Simplified Chinese, marked unconfirmed. Not advice for other games.

paid.headline: reviews
caveats: Placebo: the same competition measure 8 weeks after launch goes with 0.9% fewer reviews per launch (rate ratio 0.991, 0.989 to 0.994), against 1.0% fewer for the launch week itself (0.990, 0.987 to 0.994) on the same 66,691 games. It is about as large as the real effect or larger, so general crowding of the niche and the period explains a lot of the competition number. With both in one model, the launch week gives 0.995 (0.988 to 1.001, within noise) and the placebo 0.995. So the launch week's own effect is small at most.

Chinese holidays (rate ratios, 95% intervals): Spring Festival: games without Simplified Chinese 36% fewer reviews (0.64 (0.47 to 0.87)), games with it no clear difference (0.76 (0.58 to 1.01)); the chance test (all games pooled) gives 0.73 with p = 0.097; National Day: games without Simplified Chinese 57% fewer reviews (0.43 (0.28 to 0.67)), games with it 52% fewer reviews (0.48 (0.24 to 0.94)); the chance test (all games pooled) gives 0.50 with p = 0.005. In the review-count model the extra effect of Simplified Chinese is 1.20 (0.80 to 1.78) for Spring Festival and 1.10 (0.64 to 1.90) for National Day: no clear difference, but the intervals are wide, so a difference is not ruled out. In the "any reviews" part, games with Simplified Chinese launched during Spring Festival were less likely to get any review than other games launched then (extra odds ratio 0.72 (0.56 to 0.93)). 9 of the 9 holiday windows overlapped another Steam event (a sale, Next Fest or a themed fest), and there are only 5 Spring Festival and 4 National Day windows, so the week-clustered intervals overstate how sure this is. Not a general rule. Show Chinese holidays only as calendar context for games that support Simplified Chinese, marked unconfirmed. Not advice for other games.

The hurdle model's count part (how many reviews, given at least one) has no stable fit on this data, so it is left out. A plain count model on the games with reviews is reported instead; it is not corrected for the missing zeros.
